add_block.new_heading: What does festive catering in Dubai include?
new_paragraphs: Festive catering in Dubai from myCHEF is a full-service arrangement: a chef, the food and the people to run the evening, not just a tray dropped at the door. Every booking covers menu design tuned to the occasion, a vetted chef cooking on site, trained service staff, plating, setup and a complete cleanup. Because we work as a private festive chef service instead of a fixed-menu caterer, the food is built around your taste and guests instead of a printed list. You choose the format — a relaxed buffet, a plated dinner or live stations — and the same team handles it end to end. That is what separates proper festive catering services in Dubai from a supermarket platter: the kitchen comes to you, and the whole experience is managed so the host never has to leave the room.

add_block.new_heading: Festive catering for weddings, corporate parties and family gatherings
new_paragraphs: Festive catering for events in Dubai scales from an intimate family dinner to a company year-end gala, and the format shifts with the occasion. For homes and villas we set up festive home catering in Dubai — the chef works from your kitchen, cooks to order and leaves it spotless. For businesses, corporate festive catering in Dubai covers office parties, client dinners and Christmas or Diwali gatherings, with canapés and buffets that feed a room quickly or plated service for a seated dinner. Festive party catering in Dubai handles the louder celebrations: grazing tables, sharing feasts and dessert spreads for birthdays, engagements and community get-togethers that fall over the festive season. Whatever the setting, one coordinator manages the menu, timing and staffing, so a 12-person dinner and a 120-guest party each run to the same standard.

add_block.new_heading: What is on a festive menu in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: A festive menu in Dubai from myCHEF is bespoke, so the starting points below are shaped to your guests instead of served as-is. Popular festive food catering in Dubai includes roast turkey, slow-cooked lamb and beef feasts, holiday grazing boards, hot and cold canapés, and seasonal desserts such as yule log, mince pies, kunafa and baklava for Eid and Ramadan tables. Arabic mezze, biryanis and Indian sweets suit Diwali; a classic three-course plated dinner suits New Year. The chef balances crowd-pleasers with a few standout courses, and adjusts richness and portion sizes for the time of year. Every dish is prepared fresh on the day — nothing reheated from a central kitchen — which is why the menu is agreed in a short planning call instead of picked from a rigid template.

add_block.new_heading: Can you handle dietary needs and festive styling?
new_paragraphs: Yes — dietary requirements and presentation are planned in from the first conversation, not bolted on. Vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, nut-free, dairy-free and fully halal festive menus are all available, and the chef can run parallel options so mixed-diet tables are served without fuss. On styling, your chef plates to the setting: rustic sharing boards for a villa feast, clean fine-dining plating for a seated gala, or a decorated dessert table and grazing spread for a party. Live stations — a carvery, a canapé pass or a dessert cart — add movement to bigger rooms. Logistics are handled too: the team arrives early, brings its own equipment where a kitchen is limited, works around your timeline and clears everything at the end. The aim is that the food looks like the occasion, whatever the occasion is.

The carvery is worth singling out, because it is the one live station that goes anywhere. There is no flame, no fuel and no extraction to arrange, so a whole roast turkey or a slow-cooked lamb shoulder can be carved in a villa dining room, in a tower apartment, on a rooftop terrace, on a beach, at a desert camp or on a yacht deck — all settings where a charcoal grill, a tandoor or a fryer would each need their own sign-off first. What the carvery does need is a hot-holding plan: the joint is roasted in the licensed partner kitchen, moved under temperature control and held on the board under a lamp, which is what decides how it eats at hour two on a Dubai evening. So when a venue says no to live fire, this is the station that replaces it, and no guest at the table reads it as the lesser option.

add_block.new_heading: How much does festive catering cost in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: Festive catering in Dubai starts from AED 120 per person for a seasonal buffet or drop-off spread, rises to about AED 150 for premium menus, grazing tables, canapés and live stations, and sits at AED 700 to AED 950 per person once a vetted chef cooks and serves on site through the evening. That gap is the whole decision: at AED 120 you are buying the food and the presentation, and at AED 700 you are buying a kitchen and a service team in your house. Minimums are 10 guests on delivered formats, 20 on a buffet, and AED 900 on any order. For set occasions, festive catering packages in Dubai run from AED 1,200, with larger multi-course and multi-station builds at AED 2,400, AED 3,600, AED 4,500 and AED 5,500 depending on scale. That range means both affordable festive catering in Dubai for a simple family dinner and luxury festive catering in Dubai for a full gala sit under one roof. Festive catering prices and cost in Dubai are typically quoted itemised — see our Dubai catering price guide or send your numbers for a line-by-line quote.

For Eid and Ramadan tables, Layla Hassan leads Arabic and halal festive menus, while Matteo Moretti builds the pastry and dessert spreads. Alongside festive catering we have delivered villa weddings, yacht celebrations and corporate galas in Dubai. Real client reviews for Festive catering are published as events happen.

add_block.new_heading: Christmas, New Year, corporate hospitality — and where we can actually reach
new_paragraphs: The festive season in Dubai is three seasons stacked on top of each other, and they do not plan alike. For Christmas catering in Dubai the roast is the constraint: a whole turkey or a large joint cooks to a fixed clock and cannot be hurried, and the dates either side of 25 December fill first, so a Christmas booking wants noticeably more notice than an ordinary dinner. The full Christmas menu lives on our Christmas catering page, as Eid and Ramadan have their own. New year catering in Dubai is the opposite problem, because the food has to survive a long night: an early plated dinner, or grazing and canapés that hold their looks for hours, both beat a hot buffet timed at midnight. Corporate hospitality catering in Dubai runs across both — client dinners, hospitality suites and year-end thank-yous, where the guest list matters more than the headcount and a named chef with a fixed run-sheet is worth more than volume.

On coverage, we are a Dubai operation and would rather say so than imply otherwise. Christmas catering in Abu Dhabi is outside the area we serve as standard. Whether a partner can travel there for a particular date and party size is a question we will answer straight, before you plan anything around it.
